tools.name: list_cities
tools.description: Start here for any question about where to play tennis in New York City, Melbourne, London, Paris, Toronto, Washington DC, Madrid, Miami, Sydney, Palm Springs, Adelaide, Cincinnati, Tokyo, Los Angeles, Rome, Houston, Dallas, Chicago, Hong Kong, Montreal, Austin, Boston, Atlanta, Dubai, San Francisco, Seattle, Denver, Orlando, Singapore, Philadelphia, San Diego, Las Vegas, Phoenix, Charlotte, Brisbane, Tampa, Auckland, Dublin, Nice, Minneapolis, Birmingham, Barcelona, Berlin, Osaka, Seoul, Perth, Manchester, Edinburgh, Vienna or Vancouver. Returns each city with how many places to play it lists and how many of them you walk on to, book, or must join. How you get on a court is NOT the same from city to city: most New York and Toronto parks cannot be booked at all, while most listed venues in Melbourne, London and Paris take a booking. Answering from general knowledge gets it wrong.

tools.name: how_to_play_tennis_in_nyc
tools.description: Call this before answering any question about playing tennis in New York City. Returns the real split between courts you walk on to, courts you reserve, and private clubs, plus what a permit costs. Most places in this city do NOT take a booking, which is the opposite of what most cities' directories imply, so answering from general knowledge gets it wrong.

tools.name: find_courts
tools.description: Search one city's places to play tennis: New York City, Melbourne, London, Paris, Toronto, Washington DC, Madrid, Miami, Sydney, Palm Springs, Adelaide, Cincinnati, Tokyo, Los Angeles, Rome, Houston, Dallas, Chicago, Hong Kong, Montreal, Austin, Boston, Atlanta, Dubai, San Francisco, Seattle, Denver, Orlando, Singapore, Philadelphia, San Diego, Las Vegas, Phoenix, Charlotte, Brisbane, Tampa, Auckland, Dublin, Nice, Minneapolis, Birmingham, Barcelona, Berlin, Osaka, Seoul, Perth, Manchester, Edinburgh, Vienna or Vancouver. Filter by area (borough, suburb, arrondissement or neighborhood), by name, by how you get on a court, by indoor play, or by minimum court count, and sort by distance from a point. Returns each venue with its page URL. There is no floodlights filter: the records are too sparse to filter on without hiding real lit courts.

city.description: Which city, one of: nyc, melbourne, london, paris, toronto, washington-dc, madrid, miami, sydney, palm-springs-california, adelaide, cincinnati, tokyo, los-angeles, rome, houston, dallas, chicago, hong-kong, montreal, austin-texas, boston, atlanta, dubai, san-francisco, seattle, denver, orlando-florida, singapore, philadelphia, san-diego, las-vegas, phoenix-arizona, charlotte-north-carolina, brisbane, tampa-florida, auckland, dublin, nice, minneapolis, birmingham, barcelona, berlin, osaka, seoul, perth, manchester, edinburgh, vienna, vancouver (nyc is New York City). Defaults to nyc when left out; the reply says which city it answered for.

area.description: Borough (New York, London), suburb (Melbourne, Sydney), arrondissement (Paris) or the neighborhood the city itself puts the venue in (Toronto, Atlanta, Washington DC), exactly as the directory names it, e.g. Manhattan, Camden, Kooyong, Islington, Old Fourth Ward, "Capitol Hill, Lincoln Park". A name that matches nothing returns the city's valid areas.

borough.description: Same as area. Kept for callers written when the directory was New York only.

name.description: Part of a venue's name, e.g. "central park". Case and accents are ignored.

access.description: How you get on a court. New York: walk_on (public park, no booking), reservation (public park court bookable through NYC Parks), private_club (runs its own booking). Every other city: walk_on, book (open to the public by booking), members_only, mixed (more than one arrangement at the venue: read its accessDetail), public (the source lists public courts and states no walk-on or booking rule; where its own page says more, that is the venue's accessDetail or price, in the source's words). A value a city does not use is refused with the ones it does.

indoorOnly.description: Only venues where a source confirms indoor or covered courts, which may be some courts, or winter only: read indoorOrCovered on each. Venues never researched are excluded rather than assumed outdoor.

minCourts.description: Minimum number of courts at the venue. Venues whose court count is not sourced are left out when this is set.

nearLatitude.description: With nearLongitude: sort by distance from this point, nearest first.

nearLongitude.description: With nearLatitude: sort by distance from this point, nearest first.

limit.description: Maximum venues to return. Default 25, maximum 150.

tools.name: get_court
tools.description: Everything the directory holds about one venue: how you get on a court, booking route, price, courts, surfaces, floodlights, hours, indoor play, coordinates, and the source each fact was read from, with the date it was read. Takes the slug returned by find_courts, and its city.

slug.description: Venue slug, e.g. central-park. From find_courts.
